C

Power is given by P = V²/R. Resistance is R = ρL/A. Since the material (ρ) and diameter (A) are the same, resistance is proportional to length (R ∝ L). Halving the length (L → L/2) halves the resistance (R → R/2). With the same potential difference V, the new power is P' = V²/(R/2) = 2(V²/R) = 2P. Thus, the power dissipated is 2 × 1000 W = 2000 W.

question.html: A potential difference across a wire of length L dissipates 1000 W. A second wire of the same material and diameter has length L/2. What is the power dissipated in the second wire with the same potential difference across it?
